engines.name: Trainer scouting report
engines.what: The type matrix, bulk, the four sliders (authored and measured), tags and the written plan, every sentence a phrase rule.
engines.next: Variants you save in the Scouting Lab land in the Variants tab; say which to keep and Claude writes them into canon/trainers.json.

engines.name: Role engine
engines.what: What job each build does (34 roles), scored from stat shape, nature, EVs, item, ability, typing and move categories.
engines.next: Role weights live in roles.json; the Scouting Lab can move the confidence thresholds, not the weights yet.

engines.name: Playsheet
engines.what: Career tags, the ace, who they go to when even, ahead and behind, the type read, combos, signature moves and the aggression ratio.
engines.next: Observations on film feed it (canon/observations.jsonl); only Ash, Gary and Paul have film so far.

engines.name: Exposure
engines.what: Where your team is exposed against theirs: their attack types against your rows, and their side against your soft rows.

engines.name: Role-to-build solver
engines.what: Builds a set for a role from what a species can learn: EV templates, items, the role engine as the judge.
engines.next: Needs each species' learnable pool per game in the browser (large); worth it once the role weights settle.

engines.name: Battle engine: fights, plans and calls
engines.what: Plays every one-on-one out with Smogon's damage calculator: plans, maximin, the games' own trainer AI, what changed the result.
engines.next: Runs in the browser with Smogon's calculator; the parity test holds it to Python section for section. Not modeled yet: switching, hazards, doubles (docs/SCOUTING_ENGINE.md).

engines.name: Advance reports, self-scout, game plans, lineups
engines.what: The Journey Scouting File: member cards, call sheets per opponent, advance reports, game plans, play calls by situation.
engines.next: Every lineup's file is built live (Advance scouting checks it against the last Python run). Coach settings in canon/lineups.json are empty: try some in the Battle Lab.

engines.name: Coach profile
engines.what: Eight sliders measured from a lineup's play against the field (pace, punch, run/pass, build-up, sustain, disruption, risk, script).
engines.next: Measured live against the cached usage-field baseline; a new field needs a Python run to rebuild the baseline.

engines.name: What-if league
engines.what: Every lineup against every other, one-on-ones played out.
engines.next: About ten seconds in the Battle Lab; your edited lineup plays alongside the originals.

engines.name: Benchmarks
engines.what: The 38 cartridge opponent teams from the pret disassemblies and the 1v1 grid.
engines.next: The opponent teams are data (read from the disassemblies in Python); the grid against them is played live.

engines.name: Trainer Library
engines.what: Every notable trainer of the five games read from the pret data (350 encounters), joined with the authored ones: identities and versions, evidence per field, two lenses, collections with rules and version stamps.
engines.next: Benchmarks run in the browser (24_library.html over the battle engine); the Ace collections give the Ace test's rates (app/test_library.mjs). Not yet: the Battle Frontier, manga versions, 6v6.

engines.name: Poké Balls
engines.what: All 25 balls of Gens I-IV: which games have each and under what name, what each does read from that game's catch code (the games' bugs named), the games' own descriptions, how you get each, the Apricorns, the interior directions.
engines.next: Every number is re-checked against the pinned decompilations on every build (balls.check()). Pictures: the Dream World art or sprites until you upload your own; no image model is open to this project.

engines.name: Catch engine
engines.what: One throw's chance worked out each era's own way (Crystal's byte arithmetic, Gens 3-4's shake checks, HeartGold's Apricorn balls), with each generation's own catch rates.
engines.next: Runs in the browser (33_capture.html), held to Python by app/test_capture_parity.mjs. Wild max HP assumes IV 15 and no EVs; Safari rocks and bait aren't modelled.

engines.name: Equipment
engines.what: 28 pieces of trainer gear beyond the balls in the games' own words, with your inventory per game (My Gear).
engines.next: Saving your gear needs the updated WebApp.gs (My Gear). What each connects to in the field and homestead comes with Phase 7.

engines.name: Stat math
engines.what: Real stats by generation (Gen II DVs and stat experience the way Showdown reads them), Hidden Power, characteristics.

engines.name: Specimen kernel
engines.what: PID to nature, gender, ability slot and shininess; the PID search; Gen II DVs; the Showdown set and the PKHeX Batch Editor script.
engines.next: SPECIMEN_LAB.md 'not yet': met locations, ribbons and contest stats, Pokérus, writing .pk files, PID-IV methods.

engines.name: The ladder book and film
engines.what: Smogon's monthly stats and the sets real players run, read from 850 Showdown replays.
engines.next: The field studies (leads, cores, aggression on the ladder) aren't a page yet.

engines.name: Breeding engine
engines.what: Egg moves, feasibility, the shortest lineage of fathers for any egg move, timing warnings, one-egg bundles.
engines.next: The Breeder Lab's page is HeartGold/SoulSilver as its last run; the same search runs live in Breeding stock for every game.

engines.name: Breeding stock
engines.what: Whole starting sets: the hatch order from the games' code, the parents that make an exact set, the father's lineage, the four-state verdict, the line catalogue.
engines.next: Runs in the browser (23_stock.html), held to Python by app/test_stock_parity.mjs. IV and nature planning as a search, and ecology claims, come later.

engines.name: Studbook and lineage
engines.what: Every individual with its sire, dam, generation and inherited moves, checked against Gen 4's rules.
engines.next: Hatches you record in the app go to the Studbook tab; the engine reads them back when you tell Claude.

engines.name: Ranch planner, habitat, hatchery
engines.what: The census, the satellite choice, staffing, the Glasshouse, the egg schedule and the crop plan.
engines.next: The satellite choice and the stud reading are waiting on you (Your calls).

engines.name: Wilderness engine
engines.what: The first 27 capabilities' evidence: field moves, overworld abilities, Pokédex lore, type, size and habitat (the capability records build on it).
engines.next: Its Pokédex patterns were narrowed in Phase 7 (wings not used for flying, 'dangerously', 'seen from far away', a bare mention of the sea).

engines.name: Capability records
engines.what: 35 capabilities in seven areas, every species' evidence in every journey game on three axes (layer, class, status): game mechanics, Pokédex text, body shape, type, size, habitat, equipment rules; world records by individual.
engines.next: Moves a build knows are put to use in the page; machines and badges come from data_manifest/field_functions.json when it has been read.

engines.name: Survival and homestead assessments
engines.what: Cartridge readiness, world readiness against eleven scenarios with a kit, lock-and-optimise (Recommended / Potential Fits / Everything Else), comparisons without a winner, facility assessments under D-039.
engines.next: Runs in the browser (34_capability.html), held to Python by app/test_capability_parity.mjs. The optional expedition simulation is later (spec §9).

engines.name: Camp life
engines.what: Each game's food systems and who on the team forages, produces, cooks and heats.
engines.next: Its food systems feed the kit and scenarios; the Survival Lab's provisions are a Blackthorn standard.

engines.name: World records
engines.what: Authored facts about your world, proposed and approved.
engines.next: Approve or reject pending records in Your calls.

engines.name: Decision Lab (team diff)
engines.what: Runs every engine over two teams and shows what changes.
engines.next: The Scouting Lab diffs the report, the Battle Lab diffs the whole scouting file and the Survival Lab compares two set-ups; one page that runs all three side by side is next.

engines.name: Intake
engines.what: Videos, images, pages, pastes and research turned into cards of claims, applied only when approved.
engines.next: Running intake (Gemini, Bulbapedia) stays with Claude; the app shows the inbox and records your verdicts.

engines.name: Engine audit
engines.what: The engine held to outside references: Smogon's calc, the games' data, the Showdown protocol, Smogon's own files.

engines.name: Canon DB Sheet and its script
engines.what: The Sheet the app runs on, its menu, the lineage tree, record-a-hatch and the lock guard.

engines.name: Reference data
engines.what: PokeAPI, Showdown learnsets, Smogon sets and the pret disassemblies, pinned and checksummed.

screens.name: Journey
screens.note: The home page and the six chapters.

screens.name: Team, with build history side by side
screens.note: Team reports self-scout every chapter; build history (what each member ran before) isn't shown yet.

screens.name: Decision Lab: swap and diff
screens.note: Swap members and read the diff in the Scouting Lab, the Battle Lab and the Survival Lab; not yet on one page.

screens.name: Breeder Lab: target and moves to routes, chains, timing
screens.note: Any line, any Gen 2-4 game, a whole starting set: the parents, the chain, the verdict (#/breeder keeps HeartGold's per-move lineages).

screens.name: Field Matrix
screens.note: The Survival Lab: field moves (machine, badge, slot cost) and every capability for any team, against a scenario.

screens.name: Specimen Lab
screens.note: Stats, genes, the PID and the PKHeX script.

screens.name: History and sources
screens.note: Decisions, locks, world records and evidence; the legacy archive isn't in the app.
